newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel complains to Egypt over spy case insults.
newsitem.headline: Israel complains to Egypt over spy case insults.

text.p: Israel's ambassador to Cairo has complained to the Egyptian foreign ministry about anti-Israeli insults used at the trial of an Israeli suspected of spying in Egypt, the embassy said on Wednesday.

Fistfights broke out on Sunday between Egyptian lawyers at the trial of textile mechanic Azam Azam when a lawyer accused Azam's attorney of betraying Egypt and insulted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Ambassador Zvi Mazel mentioned the grave insults that were directed by some people present at the session against the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his adviser Asa'ad Asa'ad, and members of the Israeli embassy," the mission said in a statement.
Asa'ad, a leader of Israel's Druze community to which Azam belongs, has come to Cairo several times to visit Azam in prison and attend the trial which started on April 24.

"The ambassador expressed his surprise that security forces allowed this to go on for a long time without intervening and expressed his hope that such incidents do not recur because they contribute to creating an unsuitable atmosphere," the embassy said.

Azam, 35, and alleged Egyptian accomplice Emad Abdelhamid Ismail, are charged with two Israeli Druze women of making a criminal agreement to spy for Israel's secret service, Mossad. The women are being tried in absentia.

A lawyer representing the Egyptian Lawyers' Union accused Azam's attorney of being a traitor for agreeing to represent the Israeli and denied remarks by Azam's relative that they had contacted him as a possible attorney.

"I would have completely refused. I can't betray my country. When Netanyahu first came here I sent a telegram to the Israeli embassy in Cairo saying 'Leave the pure land of Egypt, you dirty person'," Mortada Mohsen said.
Mohsen's assistants and those of Azam's attorney traded punches and swore at each other as soon as the judge left the courtroom. The trial will continue on June 14.

At one point in the session, state security policemen had to encircle the bench where Israeli diplomats and Azam's family and friends were sitting to protect them from one lawyer who insisted they be moved to make room for him.
